bullets.title: WDC: Strong beat & raise, but stock -4-6% on capex/rotation concerns
bullets.body: WDC posted F1Q27 EPS $4.64 vs $4.10 consensus, revenue $4.38B vs $4.13B, GM 58.1% vs 55.9%; F2Q guidance $5.80 EPS on $5.1B revenue (both 10%+ above Street) with 60-61% GMs. Despite demand visibility extending to CY30-31, HAMR on track for H1 CY27, and customers signing LTAs through CY29-31, the stock fell 4-6% on elevated capex (above 4-6% LT target) and concern over competitor capacity ramps. MS raised PT to $668 (OW, 102% upside); Citi cut PT to $660 from $740 but maintains Buy; Mizuho cut PT to $490 from $590 (Outperform).

bullets.title: SPOT: Rallies 11%+ post-Q3; Morgan Stanley, JPM, Wells raise PTs to $660-$700
bullets.body: SPOT Q3 showed 306M premium subs (+2% Q/Q, ahead of consensus), GM 33.0% beating guidance, and Q4 operating income guided €820M vs €808M consensus. MS raised PT to $700 (OW, ~30x FY28 FCF); JPM raised to $700 (~21x FY28 FCF); Wells Fargo raised to $660 (23x FY28 EBITDA); KeyBanc raised to $690. FY27 EBITDA growth expected ~35% YoY as opex moderates; AI Remix/licensing deal with Believe/TuneCore adds optionality. Oppenheimer raised PT to $650 from $550.

bullets.title: META: Equity raise and capex scrutiny weighing on stock; Mizuho raises PT to $950
bullets.body: META planning significant Class C share raise (class structure preserves Zuckerberg control; $700B figure is theoretical max not actual need) with 'hundreds of billions' in combined equity+debt capital needs starting fall 2026; California wealth tax overhang adds complexity. Meta's five-year CDS hit a record high; stock was down ~7% Thursday. Mizuho raised PT to $950 from $750 (Outperform); Hedgeye signals bearish trend range 641-716.

bullets.title: SpaceX/tower deal: CCI +8-10%; T, VZ, TMUS -4-5% on 80K cell-site talks
bullets.body: SpaceX is in discussions with Crown Castle and other tower companies to access ~80,000 US cell sites for a terrestrial wireless network build-out, leveraging its 800MHz spectrum. CCI is identified as the prime beneficiary (US pureplay, ~40K pre-zoned sites, DISH abandonment accelerates deployment); incremental annual tower rent estimated $1-2B, adding 100-200bps to domestic organic growth. AT&T and Verizon each fell 4-5% on competitive displacement fears. Jefferies flags CCI and SBAC as clearest tower beneficiaries.

bullets.title: AI sector de-risking: Semis -6.8% worst day since June; NDX -2.6%
bullets.body: Hedge fund AI de-risking drove semis/SOX down 6.72% MTD and -14% month-over-month, with net tech exposure collapsing from >80th percentile to 25th percentile. SOXX hit 200-day MA for first time since June 2025; 22% of Semi/Hardware stocks screen oversold on 14D RSI. Catalysts include OpenAI's funding round closing at $1.25T (below $1.4T target), META capex scrutiny, and geopolitical risk. Hedgeye flags bearish trends on NVDA (205-226 range), META (641-716), GOOGL, AMZN; MSFT and AAPL retain bullish signals.

bullets.title: NOW: JPM previews Q3 beat of ~200bps on cRPO; KeyBanc stays Underweight at $85
bullets.body: JPMorgan expects ServiceNow Q3 to beat cRPO and Subscription revenue by ~200bps with guidance acceleration of ~50bps — framing it as a 'time for reacceleration' print. Separately, KeyBanc maintains Underweight on NOW at $85 PT, citing slowing bookings and acquisition integration headwinds.

bullets.title: RBLX: JPM and Opco constructive; 'bad short' framing on easier 2027 comps
bullets.body: JPMorgan views RBLX as 'very likely to beat' Q3 Bookings guidance with much easier 2027 comps, characterizing it as a 'bad short' rather than a 'good long.' Oppenheimer agrees RBLX is most insulated among gaming names from AI-enabled recompilation risks. GTA VI is a downside risk but 2D gaming prospects and algo optimization provide offsets.

bullets.title: BE (Bloom Energy): Beat and raise, but stock -2-3% on AI power trade skepticism
bullets.body: Bloom Energy Q3 beat consensus by ~15% and raised FY26 revenue guidance to $4.4-4.6B (+122% YoY) vs $4.1B prior consensus; delivered power to Oracle's Utah site in under 2 months. Stock fell 2-3% pre-market despite fundamentals as Hedgeye warns the AI power trade is rolling over amid $260B+ in canceled data center investments. ROTH maintains Neutral at $230 PT.

bullets.title: CRWV: MS cuts to Equal-Weight at $70; credit spreads +300bp, shares -30% in a month
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley initiated CRWV at Equal-Weight with $70 PT, noting credit spreads widened ~300bps since late August and shares are down over 30% in the past month. DDTL financing uncertainty for enterprise (vs hyperscaler) customers is the key risk; base case range cut to $50-$115 from $80-$131. CoreWeave's 2031 notes are yielding nearly 16%, per Hedgeye.

bullets.title: ORCL: KeyBanc bullish ahead of Oct 29 Investor Day; OCI revenue target raised to >$90B by FY30
bullets.body: Oracle raised its FY27 revenue target from $85B to >$90B with OCI expected to grow from <20% of revenue to >70% by FY30. KeyBanc is bullish ahead of the Oracle AI World/Analyst Day on October 29, expecting OCI EPS targets may accelerate despite component cost headwinds. Goldman also flags the event as a key catalyst for demand sustainability and FY28-30 targets.

bullets.title: CMCSA: MS stays EW at $27; broadband net losses worsening to -218K in 4Q
bullets.body: Comcast broadband net losses are worsening to -218K in 4Q from -200K due to fiber competition pricing at $30-40/month; broadband ARPU declining -2.5% YoY. Parks EBITDA down -15% YoY but expected to return to growth in 2H27. Peacock profitable for second consecutive quarter with 48M paid subs. NBCU/Sky separation on-track for mid-2027; buybacks paused.

bullets.title: OMC: Q3 organic revenue +7.2% vs consensus +3.4%; MS raises PT to $85, stays EW
bullets.body: Omnicom posted 3Q organic revenue growth of +7.2% vs MS estimate of ~4%, with EBITA margin expanding +200bps YoY to 18.2%. New wins include Coca-Cola North America, Novo Nordisk, CVS Health, and the 2028 LA Olympics. MS raised 2026E EPS to $10.40 and PT to $85 from $83, but maintains Equal-Weight.

bullets.title: TSLA: Optimus 3 external shipments pushed to late 2027; robot hand dexterity is bottleneck
bullets.body: Tesla Optimus production has started at Fremont but external commercial shipments are now targeted for late 2027 (below earlier market expectations) with volume guidance of 10,000-20,000 units before full commercial launch. The robot hand is identified as the main hardware bottleneck; AI5 chip integration in 2027 should boost complex behaviors. Internal deployment at Tesla factories for repetitive/dangerous tasks is the near-term focus.

bullets.title: MSFT / GOOGL / AMZN: Earnings next week; JPM and KeyBanc checks optimistic on MSFT
bullets.body: MSFT reports Q1 FY27 on October 28 (consensus EPS $4.71, revenue $90.63B) with JPM and KeyBanc noting optimistic channel checks above consensus. GOOGL reports October 28 (EPS $3.03, revenue $127.92B) and AMZN reports October 29 (EPS $1.96, revenue $202.16B). Hedgeye flags MSFT as one of only two large-cap tech names maintaining a bullish trend signal.

bullets.title: RCL stays OW at $394; NCLH downgraded to Underweight, PT $11 at JPM
bullets.body: JPMorgan downgrades NCLH to Underweight (from Neutral) cutting PT to $11 from $13 on -7.9% Q3 net yields, a 180bps unfavorable spread between net yields and NCC ex-fuel, and FY27 EPS modeled at $0.91 vs consensus $1.49. RCL stays Overweight at $394 with FY28 EBITDA margins +900bps vs pre-pandemic; fuel expenses raised ~$4M for Q3 on 20% bunker price increase.

bullets.title: EQIX / DLR / CORZ: Jefferies sees AI demand 2x data center supply through 2028
bullets.body: Jefferies forecasts new data center capacity of 12.9 GW in 2026, 18.0 GW in 2027, and 26.0 GW in 2028 vs 7.5 GW in 2025 — AI demand roughly double available capacity. DLR is preferred lower-risk exposure; EQIX benefits from scarce installed capacity; CORZ offers higher-risk/higher-upside on powered-land and leasing catalysts. Labor, supply chains, and political risk remain bottlenecks beyond power.

bullets.title: SHOP: Opco raises PT to $205 on 32-33% GMV growth vs Street 30.3%
bullets.body: Oppenheimer upgraded SHOP from $175 to $205 (Outperform) based on third-party data showing GMV growth tracking 32-33% vs Street's 30.3%; margin upside seen despite gross profit lagging, with profitability confidence driving the raise.

bullets.title: NVDA: Bearish trend signal; Jensen characterized neocloud demand as 'off the charts'
bullets.body: Hedgeye places NVDA in bearish trend range 205-226 with the stock under pressure from the broader AI de-risking. However, OPCO notes Jensen Huang characterized neocloud demand as 'off the charts' at GTC Berlin; NVDA reports November 25 with Street expecting 89% YoY EPS growth. UBS flags Big 6 Tech as a group lagging overall S&P 500 EPS growth (23.8% vs 29.7%).

bullets.title: T / VZ: Sold off 4-5% on SpaceX cell site speculation; T PT cut to $25 by MS
bullets.body: AT&T and Verizon each fell ~4-5% on the SpaceX tower deal headlines. Morgan Stanley cut T's PT to $25 (from $28) post results, noting solid fundamentals (Fiber ARPU -4% y/y but capex ~$1B lower in '27/28, FCF guide reiterated) but flagging a 6-7% sell-off as an overreaction. VZ reports Monday October 26 (consensus EPS $1.27, revenue $34.77B).

bullets.title: Earnings calendar: VZ Mon, STX Tue, GOOGL/MSFT/ETSY Wed, AMZN/INTC/FSLR Thu
bullets.body: Key universe earnings next week: VZ before open Monday (EPS $1.27e, revenue $34.77Be); STX after close Tuesday (EPS $7.42e, revenue $4.14Be); GOOGL and MSFT after close Wednesday; ETSY before open Wednesday (EPS $0.76e); AMZN and INTC after close Thursday; FSLR after close Thursday. Oracle AI World investor day also on October 29 — expected to update FY28-30 targets.
